## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tittirajātaka* (Ja 117) is a narrative included in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. Its opening canonical verse begins with the incipit *Accuggatā atibalatā* ("As died the partridge") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. The commentary frames the teaching at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivered it concerning the monk Kokālika [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. The commentary cross-references Kokālika's background story to the *Takkariyajātaka* in the *Terasanipāta*, remarking that Kokālika brought about his own ruin through his speech not only in his present lifetime but also in a past existence [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].

SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral]. In terms of text reuse and comparative literature, neither SuttaCentral nor the computational matches in DharmaNexus identify any Pali-internal reuse or cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
